summary: A Depth subscription on an NFO future: the 184-byte full packet gives a Depth frame with the trade time, OI and the five-level book; a later packet with an empty book clears every level.

notes: Worked by hand from the Kite full packet layout (zerodha-api-docs/10-websocket.md: last trade time at byte 44, OI at 48, exchange timestamp at 60, depth from 64), which the desktop decoder follows (brokers/zerodha/streaming.rs parse_packet).
Kite sends an empty book as five zero levels per side; the web and the desktop pass them on as they come.

deviations.reason: The web reads the exchange timestamp (byte 60) as ltt and sends it in epoch seconds; the packet's last trade time is at byte 44, and feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in ms.
deviations.ref: audit WEBSOCKET_AUDIT_PRIMARY_BROKERS.md, 'Zerodha Rust corrects existing web parser defects'; zerodha_websocket.py:826

deviations.reason: The web reads OI from byte 180, inside the last ask level, so it sends that level's order count and padding as OI; OI is at byte 48.
As oi: the web's value comes from byte 180.
